thread:
matt: Kicking off the change window canary for service-router v3.4.1 -> routing eu-west. Shifting 10% traffic to canary. SLOs to watch: p95 < 150ms, 5xx < 0.5%.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: canary_id=canary-4409876543, target=service-router:v3.4.1, traffic=10%, strategy=staggered-10m. Link: https://deploys.redwood.internal/canary/4409876543 :robot_face:
ana: On it — I'll keep an eye on slo-dashboard and traces. Ping me if we see sustained 5xx or p95 drift.
luca: Quick FYI: I already see a small p95 bump on embeddings-route (eu-west) +40ms vs baseline, no 5xx yet. KV cache hit rate reported down to ~55% (was ~98% pre-canary).
jen: I see an alert in the routing cluster: increased 502s from the kvcache layer in the last 60s. Not huge (0.3%) but trending up. @matt @ana
matt: Good catch. Can we confirm whether failures are concentrated on long-sequence requests or uniform? If 5xx > 1% sustained for 3m we pause. Also no auto-rollforward until we clear canary.
ana: Looking at traces -> long-seq embedding requests (>1024 tokens) have most of the tail. Short requests p95 steady. Stacktrace snippets show KV timeout on ttl lookup.
luca: pasted sample metrics:

```
kv_cache_hit_rate: 55% -> 52% (since canary)
embed_route_p95: 210ms (long-seq), 125ms (short)
5xx_rate: 0.32% -> 0.68% (last 2m)
```
deploy-bot: Policy check: canary-4409876543 p95_threshold_exceeded=true (p95>180ms), auto-pause threshold met -> initiating traffic pause.
jen: Pause makes sense. Initiating immediate pause and flagging rollback candidate. I'll start the rollback checklist, but holding until we confirm root cause.
matt: Agreed. Ana, can you run a quick diff of model artifact/quantization differences between v3.4.1 and v3.4.0? KV behavior changed in last patch?
ana: Running diff now. Preliminary: attention cache prefetch tweak + new kv-eviction heuristic in v3.4.1. That could explain cache miss storm on long-seq patterns.
luca: If it's the eviction heuristic, we should be able to mitigate by temporarily increasing cache size or reverting that heuristic. Can we patch config and repro the hit-rate quickly?
matt: Do quick config bump first (increase cache window), try to recover hit-rate. If that doesn't drop p95 back under 150ms within 5m, rollback to v3.4.0 and pin.
ana: Applied config: `kvcache.window=2m -> 5m` via runtime flag on canary. Monitoring now.
sre-bot: Observability alert: canary-4409876543 p95 back to 142ms (3m after config change). 5xx dropping to 0.18%.
jen: Nice. Looks like config change helped. Recommend keeping canary paused and run extended 15m burn to validate before resuming traffic shift.
matt: Agreed. Keep canary paused, run 15m soak. Ana, add a note to release docs about the kv eviction heuristic and the temporary recommended config tweak.
ana: Will do. Draft release note line: "Hotfix: KV cache eviction heuristic in v3.4.1 can reduce cache hit rates for long-sequence workloads; recommended interim config: kvcache.window=5m until v3.4.2." I'll attach trace IDs.
luca: After soak if metrics stable, we can opt to either proceed with canary or rollback+ship patch. Given impact, I'd prefer patch branch and a second canary with quantization diff disabled.
matt: Good plan. For now: paused, soak 15m, no rollforward. If stable -> proceed with targeted second canary that disables the heuristic. If not stable -> rollback and pin v3.4.0. Communicate final decision in this thread.
jen: I'll update incident tracking and notify CS about possible downstream note. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: Canary paused (traffic -> 0%). Soak timer started (15m). canary_state=PAUSED, canary_id=canary-4409876543.
matt: Thanks team. Quick post-action: remember to add a short note in release notes and the changelog about runtime config knob and the follow-up patch plan. :thumbsup:
ana: Done — release notes updated draft and PR opened: https://git.redwood/release-notes/PR-1234
luca: I'll start the patch branch to revert eviction heuristic and run unit tests.
jen: Will close loop after soak and summarize in #all-hands follow-up if we end up rolling back.
matt: Closing thread for now, will post update in ~15m. Thanks.
